scope_caveat: GOVERNING-PROFILE DISCREPANCY, carried forward from Pass 0/Pass 1 (not adopted here): this assessment is produced under the governing `faa` profile as directed, but the source tree contains no aviation/NAS/FAA content of any kind. It is the publicly published, MIT-licensed 'Gilded Rose Refactoring Kata' (README.md, attributed to @TerryHughes/@NotMyself, https://github.com/NotMyself/GildedRose) — a 172-line C# console app that models a retail inn's nightly inventory update, with no HTTP listener, database, scheduler, or GUI. src/GildedRose.Console/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs additionally asserts AssemblyCompany('DSHS') and Copyright 'DSHS 2015', a THIRD, non-FAA attribution. catalog.json (Pass 0) and structural-analysis.json (Pass 1) both already flagged this independently and recommended stakeholder confirmation before downstream use; this artifact does not resolve that question and treats every persona/adoption/accessibility figure below as conditional on it. SEPARATE GAP: Methodology §4 of this skill directs composition with the accessibility-checker sub-skill via a 'Sub-Skill Output Contract' that this producing agent's system prompt is supposed to reproduce verbatim (exact output path + schema). No such section, and no accessibility-checker schema, was present anywhere in the system prompt or dispatch bundle actually supplied for this run. Rather than invent a path/schema for a sub-skill this agent cannot correctly invoke, accessibility_findings below is this assessor's own direct, transparent read of the one discovered surface — not accessibility-checker output — and per gate_decision_note should be superseded by a real checker composition once the missing contract is supplied.

review_asks.why: If this application_id has real operational users beyond a kata participant/build-verifier, or does not actually map to an FAA-owned production system at all, every downstream persona-dependent artifact (adoption baseline, training-debt scoring, Rationalization's UX-overlap comparison) will be built on a fictional user base.

confidence.rationale: High confidence in what the source literally shows (one console entry point, no auth, one git commit) but low confidence that this represents a real, in-scope FAA application population worth basing a persona/adoption baseline on at all — that determination needs a stakeholder, not more static analysis.

review_asks.assessment: Only one persona could be derived from source: a single local console operator who builds and runs GildedRose.Console.exe interactively and presses a key to exit. This is inferred entirely from code structure (Program.cs's console Main(), no argument parsing, no authentication) and from the README's framing of the repository as a refactoring-kata exercise — there is NO usage telemetry, login system, audit log, or role/permission model anywhere in this application to measure or corroborate that inference. Every adoption_baseline and training_state figure in this artifact is consequently either an explicit 'instrumentation gap' or derived only from the repository's single 2017 commit, not from observed usage. Separately, and independent of the persona question itself: Discovery's Pass 0 and Pass 1 outputs for this application_id both already flagged that the source tree contains no aviation/FAA/NAS content (it is the publicly published, MIT-licensed 'Gilded Rose Refactoring Kata'), while an embedded AssemblyInfo.cs attribute separately claims a different, non-FAA company ('DSHS'). This assessment proceeds under the governing `faa` profile as directed, but a reviewer should confirm whether this application_id is genuinely in scope for FAA Discovery before the persona/adoption baseline below is used for any downstream decision.
review_asks.reasoning: Evidence for the persona: src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:8-35 (console Main, args parameter never read, no auth); README.md ('Your task is to add the new feature to our system...'); structural-analysis.json interface-inventory (authentication: none; human_facing: true; kind left 'unknown' because no closed vocabulary value fits an interactive-but-unscheduled console entry point). Evidence for the profile/scope doubt: catalog.json open_questions[0]-[1]; structural-analysis.json open_questions[0]; src/GildedRose.Console/Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:11,13 (AssemblyCompany/Copyright = 'DSHS'/'DSHS 2015'); the repository holds exactly one git commit, dated 2017-03-28, with no remote and no FAA-related history.

ui_inventory.name: GildedRose.Console.exe interactive console session
ui_inventory.technology: System.Console.WriteLine (stdout) / System.Console.ReadKey (stdin); no GUI toolkit, no web framework, no markup of any kind
ui_inventory.user_population: Single local operator per invocation; no roles, no authentication, and no concurrent-user or multi-session concept exists anywhere in the code
ui_inventory.notes: The application's only human-facing surface, and its only interface of any kind (Pass 1 interface-inventory counts: total 1, human_facing 1, machine_facing 0). It writes one banner line ('OMGHAI!') to stdout, then blocks indefinitely on System.Console.ReadKey() until any key is pressed, then exits. There is no page, form, menu, or navigable screen — six hard-coded inventory items are processed identically on every run. Evidence: src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:8-35; artifacts/discovery-structural-analysis/structural-analysis.json interface-inventory entry 'GildedRose.Console.exe command-line invocation'.

personas.name: Local console operator (kata participant / build verifier)
personas.estimated_headcount: unknown — no telemetry, login system, or role model exists to count distinct users; every invocation is a single interactive process run by whoever executes the compiled EXE at a terminal
personas.evidence: src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:8-35 shows the only entry point is a console Main() with no argument parsing (the args parameter is declared but never read, Program.cs:8), no authentication or authorization of any kind (a grep for Authenticate|Login|Identity|Principal across all tracked files returned zero matches, per structural-analysis.json interface-inventory), and a blocking System.Console.ReadKey() (Program.cs:33) that requires one human physically present at an interactive terminal per run. README.md frames the whole repository as a coding-kata exercise ('Your task is to add the new feature to our system...') rather than describing an operational business role.
personas.typical_workflow: Clone the repository, run build.bat, execute the compiled GildedRose.Console.exe, observe the 'OMGHAI!' banner and (typically in a debugger/IDE, per the kata's intent) the six seeded Item values before and after UpdateQuality() runs exactly once, then press any key to exit. There is no repeat-usage session model, no menu navigation, and no data entry: the same hard-coded item list (Program.cs:14-27) is processed identically on every run.
